title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Regulating Online Litigation Work during the Prevention and Control of the COVID-19 Pandemic
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Strengthening and Regulating Online Litigation Work During the Period of COVID-19 Prevention and Control

Fa [2020] No. 49

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

To thoroughly implement the series of important instructions of General Secretary Xi Jinping on the prevention and control of the COVID-19 pandemic, to resolutely implement the decisions and deployments of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, to effectively prevent and control the COVID-19 pandemic, to genuinely protect the life, health, and safety of the people, to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of parties, to provide strong judicial guarantees for pandemic prevention and control by promoting online litigation, and to ensure that online litigation activities are standardized and orderly, the following notice is hereby given regarding the relevant work of online litigation in the people's courts during the pandemic prevention and control period.

1. People's courts at all levels shall raise their political standing, fully recognize the importance and severe situation of pandemic prevention and control, effectively enhance their sense of responsibility and urgency, base themselves on their adjudication functions, and strive to serve and safeguard the overall situation of pandemic prevention and control work. They shall take the in-depth promotion of online litigation as an important measure to resolutely win the people's war, the overall war, and the war of resistance against the pandemic. They shall actively rely on online litigation platforms such as China Mobile Micro Court, the Litigation Service Network, and the 12368 Litigation Service Hotline, and comprehensively carry out online litigation activities such as online case filing, mediation, evidence exchange, trial, pronouncement of judgment, and service, effectively meeting the judicial needs of the people during the pandemic prevention and control period, and ensuring the stable and orderly operation of the trial work of the people's courts.

2. When promoting online litigation, people's courts at all levels shall not only fully consider factors such as the type of case, the degree of difficulty, and the priority and urgency, but also effectively protect the legitimate litigation rights and interests of the parties, respect the parties' choice of case handling mode, and comprehensively inform them of the rights, obligations, and legal consequences of online litigation. If the parties agree to handle the case online, the consent shall be confirmed and recorded in the information system to ensure the legal validity of the relevant litigation activities. If the parties do not agree to handle the case online and apply for an adjournment according to law, the people's court shall grant the adjournment and shall not force the application of online litigation. If the case meets the provisions of the procedural law concerning the suspension of proceedings, the people's court may suspend the proceedings.

3. People's courts at all levels shall actively guide all litigation participants to carry out online litigation activities in an orderly manner according to law, vigorously improve the online processing procedures and online litigation rules, formulate and publish comprehensive, clearly guided, simple and easy-to-operate online litigation operation guidelines, the relevant content of which shall not breach the provisions of current laws and judicial interpretations. Courts carrying out pilot work on the simplification and分流 reform of civil procedure shall, within the scope authorized by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, strictly follow the "Implementation Measures of the Supreme People's Court for the Reform Pilot on Simplification and Diversion of Civil Procedure" (Fa [2020] No. 11, hereinafter referred to as the "Pilot Implementation Measures") to promote online litigation work. Higher people's courts at all levels shall conduct a comprehensive review of the online litigation rights and obligations notices, online litigation rules, and online litigation operation guidelines formulated by courts within their jurisdiction to ensure that the relevant content is legal, accurate, and operable.

4. When handling cases online, people's courts at all levels shall ensure the authenticity of the identities of all litigation participants. Identity authentication shall be completed online through methods such as comparison of certificates and credentials, biometric identification, and association with real-name mobile phone numbers. Special accounts for the litigation platform shall be provided to all litigation participants, achieving consistency matching of "person, case, and account."

5. Where a party or its agent ad litem submits an application for case filing through online means, the people's court shall review it within seven days after receiving the materials for filing. If the conditions for filing a lawsuit prescribed by law are met, the case shall be registered and filed; if the submitted materials do not meet the requirements, the people's court shall promptly require corrections through the online litigation platform, and shall inform the party at one time of the content and deadline for corrections. If corrections are not made within the time limit, the filing materials shall be returned. If the conditions for filing a lawsuit are not met, and after the people's court explains, the plaintiff insists on continuing the lawsuit, a ruling or decision shall be made not to accept or not to file the case.

If a party or its agent ad litem has genuine difficulty in submitting filing materials online, they may choose to submit the filing materials to a nearby people's court. The relevant people's court shall promptly handle the filing procedures in accordance with the working mechanism and procedures for cross-regional case filing.

6. People's courts at all levels shall increase the efforts to resolve conflicts and disputes during the pandemic prevention and control period. Relying on the online diversified dispute resolution platform, they shall strengthen coordination and cooperation with relevant units such as judicial administrative departments and bar associations, further integrate and gather dispute resolution forces such as people's mediation, administrative mediation, industry mediation, and lawyer mediation, and effectively promote the online resolution of conflicts and disputes. They shall actively improve the mechanism for linking litigation and mediation, and increase judicial protection for online diversified dispute resolution. If a party applies for judicial confirmation of an online mediation agreement and meets the legal conditions, the people's court shall promptly confirm it according to law.

7. If a party or its agent ad litem submits litigation materials and evidence materials in electronic form, and these are approved by the people's court, the paper originals may no longer be submitted. If the party or its agent ad litem submits paper materials by mail or other means, the people's court shall promptly scan and input them into the case handling system. The original paper materials submitted shall be promptly filed and archived. The people's court shall actively guide the parties and their agents ad litem to submit electronic materials, providing them with platform support and technical convenience.

8. People's courts at all levels shall actively promote and orderly regulate online trials, comprehensively considering factors such as technical conditions, case circumstances, and the willingness of the parties to determine whether to adopt the online trial method. Civil, commercial, and administrative cases can generally be tried online. However, online trials are not applicable in cases where both parties do not agree to an online trial, the technical conditions for an online trial are not available, or there is a need to verify identities on-site, check originals, or examine physical evidence. In criminal cases, remote video methods may be used to interrogate the defendant, pronounce judgments, and hear cases of commutation of sentence and parole. For simple criminal cases applying summary procedures or fast-track procedures, cases of leniency for pleading guilty and accepting punishment, and criminal cases hindering pandemic prevention and control, remote video methods for trial may be explored.

Online trial activities shall follow the relevant provisions of procedural laws and judicial interpretations, fully protecting the litigation rights of the parties, including the right to apply for withdrawal, to present evidence, to cross-examine, to make statements, and to debate. Online trials shall be conducted by online video, and shall not be conducted in written or audio form.

When a people's court conducts an online trial, it shall generally be conducted within a courtroom. If, due to the needs of pandemic prevention and control, a judge genuinely needs to conduct an online trial in another location, the judge shall report to and obtain approval from the president of the court, and ensure that the trial venue is solemn and serious and that trial etiquette is standardized. The people's court shall, referring to the relevant provisions of the "Rules of the People's Court of the People's Republic of China," strengthen guidance to participants in online trials, clarify the discipline of online trials, and ensure that the trial process is safe, civilized, standardized, and orderly.

If a party expressly agrees to an online trial but fails to appear on time or withdraws without authorization during the trial, unless it is confirmed that the reason is a network failure, equipment damage, power outage, or force majeure, it may be deemed as "failure to appear in court" and "withdrawal during the trial," and shall be handled according to the relevant provisions of procedural laws and judicial interpretations respectively.

The people's court shall actively use voice recognition technology to simultaneously generate electronic trial transcripts, which shall be confirmed online by the trial personnel, judge assistants, court clerks, parties, and other litigation participants to ensure the validity of the online trial activities. The entire process of the online trial shall be recorded in audio and video and stored for archiving in accordance with the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Audio and Video Recordings of Court Trials."

9. During the pandemic prevention and control period, people's courts at all levels may, based on technical conditions and work needs, allow judges to remotely access electronic case files, deliberate on cases, and draft and submit written judgments, etc., but shall strictly comply with the relevant provisions on electronic case file management and confidentiality.

10. People's courts at all levels shall increase the application of electronic service, improving the quality and efficiency of service. With the consent of the person to be served, litigation documents and evidence materials submitted by the parties may be served by electronic means such as China Mobile Micro Court, China Judicial Process Information Online, the nationwide unified service platform, fax, email, and instant messaging accounts.

Courts included in the reform pilot on simplification and分流 of civil procedure shall conduct electronic service work in an orderly manner according to law in accordance with the provisions of Articles 24 to 26 of the "Pilot Implementation Measures." For courts not included in the pilot, regarding the conditions for applying electronic service and the standards for effectiveness, they may refer to the provisions of Articles 24 and 26 of the "Pilot Implementation Measures," but shall not use electronic means to serve judgments, rulings, or mediation statements, ensuring that the electronic service of the people's courts complies with the provisions of procedural laws and judicial interpretations.

11. People's courts at all levels shall vigorously promote the construction of a one-stop diversified dispute resolution mechanism and a one-stop litigation service center, upgrade the online litigation service platform, expand the functions of online litigation services, and provide parties and the public with comprehensive online litigation services such as litigation consultation, fee payment and refund, information inquiry, contacting judges, complaint reporting, petitions, and whistleblowing and complaints, ensuring that parties can obtain judicial information and handle litigation matters without leaving their homes, effectively reducing travel and gatherings of people, and serving the work of pandemic prevention and control.

12. The Internet Courts of Hangzhou, Beijing, and Guangzhou shall make full use of their first-mover advantages, increase exploration in aspects such as case handling platform construction, online litigation procedures, application of emerging technologies, and online litigation rules. On the basis of ensuring the full online trial of internet cases, they shall accelerate the improvement of the intelligent level of trial and enforcement work, strengthen research and application of technologies such as big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and 5G technology, explore the formation of practice samples of smart justice, and summarize and form advanced experiences that can be replicated and promoted. Based on their own functional positioning, they shall actively explore the rules of electronic litigation in the internet era, promote the improvement of substantive rules for internet judicial governance, effectively play the leading and exemplary role of internet courts in concept innovation, technological innovation, and institutional innovation, and effectively promote the legalization of cyberspace governance.

13. People's courts at all levels shall attach great importance to the promotion of online litigation work during the pandemic prevention and control period, effectively optimize concepts, deepen understanding, and change thinking, take online litigation as the basic mode for people's courts to carry out trial and enforcement work during the special period, ensure that the team does not disperse, work does not stop, and quality and efficiency do not decline, make beneficial explorations for further improving the internet judicial model, and lay a good practical foundation. The presidents of people's courts at all levels shall serve as the primary responsible persons for promoting online litigation, clarify the working ideas, rationalize the working mechanism, increase the intensity of organization and implementation, actively take the lead in handling cases online, play a leading and exemplary role, and promote online case handling as a normalized mechanism during the pandemic prevention and control period.

14. People's courts at all levels shall vigorously strengthen the construction of information technology infrastructure, actively promote and apply China Mobile Micro Court, accelerate the construction of an online litigation platform with China Mobile Micro Court as the main entrance, promote the connection of existing litigation service platforms with China Mobile Micro Court, integrate and improve various information systems, and prevent multiple developments and duplicate constructions. They shall strive to connect the internal and external networks to achieve safe and effective interaction of judicial data. Based on existing platform systems, they shall add corresponding functional modules, expand and optimize various functions of online litigation, meet practical needs, optimize the user interface, improve user experience, and ensure that the online litigation service system is integrated, efficient, and convenient.

15. Higher people's courts at all levels shall actively provide overall guidance for the promotion of online litigation by courts within their jurisdiction, formulate and issue relevant litigation rules and document templates, increase the intensity of guidance for lower-level courts, and ensure that online litigation activities are standardized, unified, legal, and orderly. They shall adhere to the principles of promoting while summarizing and researching, continuously summarize and refine the beneficial measures and experiences of courts within their jurisdiction in promoting online litigation, carefully collect existing problems and difficulties, propose specific solutions or suggestions, and promptly form work reports to submit to the Office of the Judicial Reform Leading Group of the Supreme People's Court.

February 14, 2020
